question: What is the main purpose of looking at clinical signs in tummy (gastrointestinal) problems?

options.A: To calculate the total hospital bill for the patient
options.B: To replace all lab tests and scans completely
options.C: To guess the exact day the patient will leave the hospital
options.D: To give us clues about how well the gut is working and looking

explanation: Signs and symptoms act like windows into the digestive tract, helping nurses and doctors figure out what is going wrong inside. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to catch tummy (GI) warning signs early?

options.A: It completely removes the need to give IV fluids
options.B: It means nurses can skip doing physical tummy checks
options.C: It stops things like severe bleeding or a burst gut from getting worse fast
options.D: It makes sure the patient will never need surgery

explanation: Spotting warning signs early lets your healthcare team step in before life-threatening emergencies like heavy bleeding or bowel perforation happen. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h1)

question: Which type of tummy pain is usually dull, aching, and hard to point to with just one finger?
explanation: When hollow organs stretch or cramp, they cause visceral pain. Because internal organs have fewer pain nerve endings, patients struggle to point to the exact spot. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h2)

question: A patient has sharp, severe tummy pain that hurts much worse when they move or take a deep breath. What is the most likely cause?

options.B: Slow movement in the large bowel
options.C: Normal gas movement through the colon
options.D: Stretching of a hollow organ muscle

explanation: The parietal peritoneum has lots of somatic nerve fibers that react sharply to movement and inflammation, causing that localized, sharp pain. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h2)

question: What is the correct order for examining a patient's tummy (abdomen)?
explanation: Always listen (auscultate) before you touch or press! Pressing first can change the natural bowel sounds and mess up your assessment. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h3)

question: A patient with gallbladder trouble feels pain up near their right shoulder blade. What is this called?
explanation: Referred pain happens when internal organs and skin areas share the same spinal cord pathways, tricking the brain into feeling the pain somewhere else. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h3)

question: Why are patients who vomit heavily for a long time at high risk for metabolic alkalosis?

options.A: They eat too many alkaline foods while recovering
options.B: Their lungs trap extra carbon dioxide to fix the fluid loss
options.C: Their kidneys completely stop making urine
options.D: They lose large amounts of stomach acid

explanation: Vomiting throws out hydrochloric acid from your stomach, leaving your body with extra base, which pushes your blood pH up into alkalosis. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h4)

question: Which of these signs often happens to a person right before they vomit?

options.B: Sweating and pale skin (diaphoresis and pallor)

explanation: When the vomiting center in the brain wakes up, it triggers the autonomic nervous system, often making the patient sweat, look pale, and feel warm or cold just before emesis. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h4)

question: Which body landmark separates upper GI bleeding from lower GI bleeding?
explanation: The ligament of Treitz sits right where the duodenum meets the jejunum, serving as the official dividing line for GI bleeding. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why does blood from an upper GI bleed usually turn black and tarry (melena) by the time it comes out?

options.A: The patient has been eating too many dark green vegetables
options.B: Bile acids in the large bowel bleach the blood
options.C: Stomach bacteria turn the iron bright red
options.D: Digestive enzymes and stomach acid break down the blood during its trip

explanation: As old blood travels all the way down the long digestive tract, stomach acid and enzymes break down the hemoglobin, turning it dark, sticky, and black. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h5)

question: What is the primary reason patients with chronic malabsorption develop peripheral edema?

options.A: Loss of plasma proteins leading to decreased blood oncotic pressure
options.B: Direct blockage of the lymphatic vessels inside the lower extremities
options.C: Excessive retention of salt caused by overactive adrenal glands
options.D: Increased pumping pressure generated by a weakened heart muscle

explanation: When the gut fails to absorb protein, blood albumin drops. This lowers blood oncotic pressure, allowing fluid to leak out of vessels into body tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h6)

question: Which vitamin shortage is directly linked to poor blood clotting in long-term malabsorption?
explanation: Vitamin K is a fat-soluble vitamin needed by the liver to make clotting factors. If fats aren't being absorbed, Vitamin K isn't either! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h6)

question: What is an important nursing check after a patient has an upper GI scope (endoscopy)?

options.A: Giving strong oral laxatives to clear out remaining dye
options.B: Putting warm compresses on the tummy every 15 minutes
options.C: Checking that the patient's gag reflex is back before giving food or water
options.D: Pushing the patient to eat a heavy meal right away to get their strength back

explanation: The throat spray numbs the back of the throat during the scope. If you feed them before the gag reflex returns, they could easily choke or aspirate. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h7)

question: Why is watching electrolyte levels so important for a patient with severe, ongoing diarrhea?

options.A: Gut cells need high calcium to make digestive enzymes
options.B: Rapid fluid loss causes dangerous mineral imbalances in the body
options.C: Electrolytes tell you if the patient can walk down the hall
options.D: Stool thickness depends entirely on sodium in the blood

explanation: Diarrhea flushes out lots of water and essential mineral salts, putting the patient at risk for dangerous drops in potassium and sodium that can affect the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h7)
